messages:
priya: Quick sync — we have 3 customer asks that rose to high priority: FinCorp (private deployment SLA), EduStart (edu discounts + smaller model), RetailX (reranking/latency). Need a prioritization for Q2/Q3. Thoughts on RICE + minimal canary scope?

mike: +1 on RICE. Can we surface rough numbers? I sketched something in-thread.

mike: Quick RICE calc:
```
FinCorp: reach 8 * impact 7 * conf 0.8 / effort 5 = 8.96
EduStart: reach 5 * impact 6 * conf 0.7 / effort 2 = 10.5
RetailX: reach 6 * impact 5 * conf 0.6 / effort 3 = 6.0
```

lina: Those effort numbers assume infra does VPC onboarding + KMS work. If infra needs a new automation flow, effort for FinCorp jumps to 8.

sam: If we treat EduStart as a trimmed canary (hosted API + prompt templates, no dedicated capacity), we can deliver with low infra changes. That matches the low effort number.

anna: Launch criteria proposal: 1) E2E happy path tests, 2) security sign-off for data retention, 3) docs + 2 pilot customers, 4) rollback plan. Without those we don't mark GA.

priya: Good. Impact vs effort also matters — EduStart is higher per-unit ROI and quick time-to-value. FinCorp is strategic and revenue but big infra lift and compliance gating.

product-ops: Suggest a simple queue policy while backlog is hot: allow 1 "customer-urgent" slot per sprint + 1 "strategic" slot (longer runway) and 1 "quick win" slot. Helps avoid starving infra.

lina: That policy would help. Eng capacity next two sprints is ~30 story points per squad; infra team has ~10 SP for platform work. If FinCorp is greenlit, it consumes ~6 SP/week for 6 weeks. That's a big chunk.

mike: Alternative: split FinCorp into two phases — Phase A (network peering + minimal auth) for Q3, Phase B (full KMS + audit logs) for Q4. That reduces immediate footprint.

sam: Agree. Also consider reuse: EduStart telemetry and onboarding flow can be reused by FinCorp later, lowering Phase B effort.

anna: For prioritization math, confidence numbers matter — how confident are we on reach? FinCorp might be 8 in revenue but few customers. Consider adding an "urgency" multiplier for contract expirations.

priya: Good call. FinCorp has time pressure (renewal in 6 months), so add urgency flag to scheduling but not to RICE score. Means we may need to reserve a strategic slot earlier.

product-ops: Operational note — update roadmap board with swimlanes: "canary/hosted", "dedicated/infra-heavy", "research/experiments". Then enforce the per-sprint slot policy.

devops-bot: Reminder: oncall rotation changed this week — infra oncall: @lina until 2025-12-01.

mike: Proposed decision: Ship EduStart as canary in Q2 (minimal infra), allocate strategic slot in Q3 for FinCorp Phase A, plan Phase B in Q4. RetailX deprioritized unless they convert to a paid pilot.

lina: I can commit infra to EduStart canary (1-2 SP) and FinCorp Phase A planning, but Phase A execution needs formal capacity reservation.

priya: Agreement: EduStart = Q2 canary, FinCorp = Q3 Phase A (network + auth), Phase B Q4. RetailX on hold. Action items: 1) @mike write spec for EduStart canary (scope + tests) by EOD Fri. 2) @lina raise capacity request for FinCorp Phase A in next capacity sync. 3) @anna draft launch checklist template.

sam: I'll add the EduStart quick spec template to the repo and link in the thread when done.

priya: Thanks. If anyone has blockers for the quick win, flag them here. :+1:
